ai.description: This 4–6 cm frog has a green-spotted brown back and white belly. It features a distinct, broad adhesive disc on each fingertip and a prominent, white-edged tympanum. Family: Ranidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops viridimaculatus* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, bright green spots scattered across its dorsum, which are absent in other similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: The Dahaoping Sucker Frog inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within subtropical evergreen broadleaf forests at elevations ranging from 1,200 to 1,600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Dahaoping sucker frog is primarily nocturnal, utilizing its specialized abdominal disc to cling to wet rocks in fast-flowing streams while foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops viridimaculatus* is an oviparous breeder that deposits eggs in streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops viridimaculatus* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya, inhabiting high-altitude streams between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Dahaoping Sucker Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, pulsed notes, typically heard near fast-flowing mountain streams in its forest habitat.
